Our interests include space technology, astronomy, software development, computer vision, data analysis, embedded systems, and engineering.
summary:
Arcadian SkyTracker, developed by Arcadian SpaceWorks for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, is an interactive platform for exploring SPHEREx astronomical observations.

Users can select sky coordinates, search NASA/IPAC IRSA for available observations and FITS image cutouts, or explore an offline collection of 60 real SPHEREx cutouts. An interactive timeline organizes observations by their recorded timestamps, while visualization tools allow users to inspect astronomical images and metadata.

The platform supports side-by-side and blink comparisons and can generate visual difference images for eligible observation pairs. Its comparison workflow checks observation time, detector, approximate wavelength, spatial overlap, and brightness units, while reporting PSF diagnostics.

An optional Scientific Detection Lab performs controlled synthetic-signal experiments using real SPHEREx image backgrounds.

Arcadian SkyTracker makes astronomical data easier to explore while transparently identifying the scientific calibration and validation steps required before confirming real astronomical changes.
details:
Arcadian SkyTracker - Project Details

The Problem

NASA's SPHEREx mission provides valuable infrared astronomical observations, but exploring scientific FITS files, interpreting metadata, and comparing observations can be challenging for students, educators, and astronomy enthusiasts.

Arcadian SkyTracker aims to bridge the gap between publicly available astronomical data and accessible, interactive scientific exploration.

Our Solution

Arcadian SkyTracker is an interactive web application that allows users to explore real SPHEREx observations through a visual interface.

The platform offers:

  • Interactive Sky Exploration: Users can select celestial coordinates, discover available observations, and inspect astronomical images and metadata.
  • Temporal Exploration: A timeline organizes observations by their recorded timestamps, allowing users to explore the same region across different observation periods.
  • Image Comparison: Users can compare observations side by side, switch between images using a blink view, and generate visual difference images when compatibility requirements are satisfied.
  • Scientific Compatibility Checks: The system evaluates observation timestamps, detector identity, approximate wavelength, spatial overlap, and brightness units before permitting certain comparisons. PSF diagnostics are also reported.
  • Offline Demonstration Mode: A preloaded collection of 60 real SPHEREx FITS cutouts across four astronomical targets allows users to explore the application without relying on live archive access.
  • Scientific Detection Lab: An optional experimental environment evaluates computational change-detection methods by injecting synthetic signals into copies of real astronomical image data.

Technical Implementation

The application uses a React-based frontend and a Python backend.

The frontend provides the interactive sky map, observation tables, temporal navigation, image visualization, and comparison tools.

The backend integrates with the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), processes astronomical FITS data, handles image retrieval, and performs scientific compatibility checks and image comparison operations.

For eligible observation pairs, the comparison pipeline uses celestial coordinate information to reproject images and calculate visual differences.

The offline demonstration system uses locally bundled FITS observations and accompanying previews, with integrity checks to verify the included assets.

Scientific Methodology and Limitations

Scientific accuracy and transparency are central design considerations.

Astronomical images acquired at different wavelengths, with different instrumental characteristics or calibration conditions, cannot always be meaningfully subtracted.

Arcadian SkyTracker therefore distinguishes visual exploration from scientifically validated change detection.

Although the platform can generate visual difference images, these are not automatically evidence of astronomical variability or transient discovery. Full scientific validation would require additional work, including PSF matching, photometric calibration, and source verification.

For moving astronomical targets, the platform can visualize predicted positions derived from astronomical reference data. These predictions must not be confused with independently measured object positions in SPHEREx images.

The Scientific Detection Lab provides controlled synthetic experiments, rather than confirmed detections of new astronomical phenomena.

Development and Validation

The team developed and evaluated the platform using automated backend and frontend tests, scientific validation scripts, and integrity checks on the offline astronomical dataset.

The recorded validation results include 249 passing backend tests, 9 passing frontend test files, and successful integrity validation of 60 FITS/PNG pairs.

These tests verify important software and data-handling behavior but do not establish scientific validation of real astronomical change detection.

Generative AI tools were used to assist with aspects of development, debugging, documentation, and presentation preparation. The team reviewed the resulting work and remains responsible for the implementation and scientific claims.

Impact and Future Development

Arcadian SkyTracker is intended to make NASA's astronomical data more approachable for students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers seeking an initial exploratory interface.

Future development could include scientifically calibrated difference imaging, automated candidate detection, improved image processing, and accessible explanations of astronomical observations using language models.

Our long-term vision is to transform complex astronomical data into an interactive experience that encourages exploration, scientific curiosity, and citizen participation.
